objective: Add bounded multi-evaluator consensus admission for agent reliability evidence by binding evaluator identity/key epoch, common rubric, task/trace lineage, coverage, confidence, disagreement, safety failure, and harm severity under generation/expiry/replay/tamper controls without running graders or approving releases.

research_inputs.finding: Trace debugging should precede repeatable dataset and evaluation runs when benchmarking workflow changes over time.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: The contract accepts caller-supplied evaluator receipts bound to a stable evaluation-set identity and does not execute models or graders.

research_inputs.finding: Structured trace labels can expose tool, handoff, instruction, and safety regressions, but they remain evaluation evidence.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: The ledger requires common task/trace lineage and rejects evaluator disagreement, safety failure, and harm evidence beyond policy without promoting receipts to authority.

research_inputs.finding: Agent reliability is multi-dimensional: consistency, robustness, predictability, and safety; safety deterioration should be a hard constraint rather than averaged away.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: The contract includes coverage, confidence, disagreement, safety-failure, and harm-severity gates and keeps safety checks separate from any quality score.

features: unique evaluator identity and key-epoch binding
policy generation, platform ABI, TTL and expiry binding

benchmark.scope: local Python control-plane consensus verification overhead; excludes grader execution, model invocation, network, storage, accelerators, kernel scheduling, and release approval latency

rollback.rollback_scope: remove the evaluator-consensus module, tests, runner, evidence registration, and metadata; retain prior tagged evaluation-set release

limitations: The ledger verifies caller-supplied evaluator receipts and does not run graders, independently identify evaluators, verify rubric quality, or prove that receipts reflect real traces.
Consensus between evaluators does not establish truth; it only satisfies the configured evidence-consistency policy.
The benchmark measures local Python control-plane overhead and excludes grading, model, tool, network, storage, accelerator, kernel scheduler, and approval latency.
The real-task validation is a deterministic local fixture and does not establish agent quality, general intelligence, browser autonomy, robotics, or production efficacy.
No physical accelerator, TPM, secure enclave, independent builder, live multihost deployment, or independent external security review was exercised.
This evidence does not claim AGI capability, production approval, or superiority to Linux.
